---
title: "Benchmarking the learners"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE
)
lgr::get_logger("mlr3")$set_threshold("warn")
```

This case study compares the four learners on label error and on training time. The data are simulated, so the number of sequences can grow as needed.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Simulated sequences

`simulate_task()` draws `n_seq` sequences of 200 points. Each has its own noise level between 0.5 and 5, so one penalty cannot suit them all. Odd sequences change mean once, by three times their noise level, between positions 80 and 120. They carry a `1change` label around the change and a `0changes` label before it. Even sequences are flat, with one `0changes` label.

```{r}
simulate_task = function(n_seq, n_data = 200L) {
  signal = vector("list", n_seq)
  label = vector("list", n_seq)
  for (i in seq_len(n_seq)) {
    noise = exp(runif(1L, log(0.5), log(5)))
    if (i %% 2L == 1L) {
      change = sample(80:120, 1L)
      signal[[i]] = c(rnorm(change, 0, noise), rnorm(n_data - change, 3 * noise, noise))
      label[[i]] = data.table(
        start = c(1, change - 10),
        end = c(change - 20, change + 10),
        label = c("0changes", "1change")
      )
    } else {
      signal[[i]] = rnorm(n_data, 0, noise)
      label[[i]] = data.table(start = 1, end = n_data, label = "0changes")
    }
  }
  TaskCpt$new(
    id = paste0("simulated_", n_seq), backend = data.table(signal = signal, label = label),
    target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
  )
}
```

All learners use `Kmax = 2`. The MMIT and MMIF learners are included when the mmit package is installed.

```{r}
has_mmit = requireNamespace("mmit", quietly = TRUE)
learners = list(
  lrn("changepoint.intregrcv", Kmax = 2L, n.folds = 2L, min.observations = 2L),
  lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft", Kmax = 2L)
)
if (has_mmit) {
  learners = c(learners, lrns(c("changepoint.mmit", "changepoint.mmif"), Kmax = 2L))
}
```

## Label error

Three-fold cross-validation on 80 sequences, with the same folds for every learner:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
task = simulate_task(80L)
measures = msrs(c("changepoint.label_error", "changepoint.auc"))
design = benchmark_grid(task, learners, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L))
bmr = benchmark(design)
bmr$aggregate(measures)[, .(learner_id, changepoint.label_error, changepoint.auc)]
```

The best penalty grows with the noise variance of a sequence. The features include variance estimates, so every learner can follow it. With about 53 training sequences per fold, `changepoint.intregrcv` and `changepoint.xgboost.aft` get every label right, and the tree learners miss a few.

## Training time

The timing loop trains each learner on simulated tasks of `N` = 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 sequences, three times per size, and keeps the median elapsed time from `system.time()`.

```{r}
timings = list()
for (n_seq in c(10L, 20L, 40L, 80L, 160L)) {
  set.seed(1)
  task_n = simulate_task(n_seq)
  for (learner in learners) {
    seconds = numeric(3L)
    for (r in seq_len(3L)) {
      seconds[r] = system.time(learner$clone(deep = TRUE)$train(task_n))[["elapsed"]]
    }
    timings[[length(timings) + 1L]] = data.table(N = n_seq, learner = learner$id, seconds = median(seconds))
  }
}
timings = rbindlist(timings)
dcast(timings, N ~ learner, value.var = "seconds")
```

The plot uses log scales on both axes, so a power law `seconds ~ N^b` is a straight line with slope `b`.

```{r, fig.alt = "Log-log plot of median training time against the number of sequences, one line per learner."}
ggplot(timings, aes(N, seconds, colour = learner)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "number of sequences N", y = "median training time (seconds)")
```

The slope of a least-squares line through the log-log points estimates `b` for each learner:

```{r}
timings[, .(slope = coef(lm(log(seconds) ~ log(N)))[[2L]]), by = learner]
```

A slope near 1 means training time grows linearly with the number of sequences. Every learner first computes the target intervals by running the segmentation solver on each sequence, which is linear in `N` and the same for all learners. `changepoint.xgboost.aft` grows about linearly, and the tree learners a little slower over this range. `changepoint.intregrcv` has a slope well below 1 because its time here is mostly a fixed cost: its internal cross-validation fits a whole regularisation path, which takes several seconds even for 10 sequences.
